title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed from this page and its neighbours). P is a space. M is a set of 'figures' X. Each figure has a closed support |X| ⊂ P and an open part |X|°, with ∂X = |X| \ |X|°. M carries an order ≤. Two disjointness relations are used:
- Z || X means |Z| ∩ |X| = ∅.
- Z |°| X means |Z|° ∩ |X|° = ∅.

Orthogonality data:
- cosupp° X = {Z : Z |°| X}.
- supp° X = the double orthogonal, {Y : every Z with Z |°| X also satisfies Z |°| Y}.
- φ(A) = ⋃_{Y∈A} |Y|°.

The aim, over pp. 73–75, is to show that this purely combinatorial polarity recovers the geometry: φ(supp° X) = |X|° and φ(cosupp° X) = P \ |X|°. Later (p. 75), with supp X = supp°(X̃), also φ(supp X) = |X| and φ(cosupp X) = P \ |X|. The key step, carried from p. 73, is: if |Y|° ⊄ |X|°, there is Z with Z |°| X but |Z|° ∩ |Y|° ≠ ∅.

On this page the proof splits into two cases.

Case 1: |Y|° meets ∂X. The frontier condition ∂X = ⋃_{Z<X} |Z|° gives some Z < X with |Y|° ∩ |Z|° ≠ ∅. Strata of distinct comparable figures are disjoint, so Z |°| X, and this Z works.

Case 2: otherwise. Since P \ |X|° = ∂X ⊔ (P \ |X|), the set |Y|° meets P \ |X|. Grothendieck then postulates a separation hypothesis:
- Hyp: for every X ∈ M and every x ∉ |X| there is Z ∈ M with Z || X and x ∈ |Z|.
- Equivalently: P \ |X| is the union of the |Z| (or of the |Z|°) over Z ∈ cosupp(X).

He notes that the weaker Z |°| X suffices for his purpose. In a NB, replacing Z by one of its strata, one may take x ∈ |Z|°.

The marginal remark says Hyp with || is 'too strong'. The reasonable form is Z |°| X, which admits configurations defined by (strict) inequalities. Example: the closed half-line x ≥ 0 cannot be separated from points x < 0 by figures with disjoint closures in a semi-algebraic-type setting, only by figures with disjoint interiors.

P. 75 then derives P \ |X|° = ⋃_{Z∈cosupp° X} |Z|° and goes on to the closed-support versions.

Overall this is part of Grothendieck's 1986 attempt to axiomatize a 'tame' analysis situs: a space presented by a poset of stratified figures, with the topology recovered from an orthogonality (disjointness) relation via a Galois connection.
errors: No real error. The NB (replacing Z by a stratum so that x ∈ |Z|°) is unnecessary: |Y|° is an open neighbourhood of x and x ∈ |Z| = closure of |Z|°, so |Y|° already meets |Z|°. This uses only the implicit assumption that |Z| is the closure of |Z|°.
Case 1 tacitly uses that Z < X implies |Z|° ∩ |X|° = ∅, i.e. that the open strata of M partition (a frontier-condition / stratification axiom). This is not stated on the page.

If the stratum route of the NB is used under the weak hypothesis Z |°| X, one also needs that the chosen stratum Z' ≤ Z still satisfies Z' |°| X. This holds if open strata are pairwise equal or disjoint and x ∉ |X|; it is again implicit.

ideas.what: Recovering the open/closed supports of figures from the disjointness relation |°| through a double-orthogonal (polar) closure supp° X = (X^⊥)^⊥, with φ(supp° X) = |X|°.
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity from a disjointness ('contact') relation; analogous to regular-open algebras and contact algebras in point-free topology (mereotopology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); de Vries (compingent algebras, 1962); Whitehead/de Laguna region-based geometry; Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology programme is in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; these 1986 Analysis situs notes are unpublished

ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for stratifications / CW-type posets of strata
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses stratified 'tame' spaces in general terms

ideas.what: Separation hypothesis Hyp: the complement of a figure's support is covered by figures orthogonal to it, P \ |X| = ⋃_{Z∈cosupp X} |Z|. It is weakened from closed disjointness (||) to disjointness of open parts (|°|) so as to allow sets defined by inequalities.
ideas.modern_name: A separation/regularity axiom for a basis of 'figures' (cf. separation of a closed set from a point in regular spaces; complements of definable closed sets in o-minimal structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard point-set topology; in a definable setting it is automatic

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to rebuild a tame space from a poset of figures plus a disjointness relation, using double orthogonals. This is essentially the programme of contact algebras / region-based topology (de Vries duality), developed independently in logic and mereotopology. The two literatures (Grothendieck's tame topology and point-free contact-algebra duality) are not usually linked.
missed.quote: Cette hypothèse équivaut (pour X donné) à P \ |X| = ⋃_{Z∈cosupp°(X)} |Z|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests framing Grothendieck's 'analysis situs' axioms as a de Vries / contact-algebra style duality restricted to tame (e.g. o-minimal or semi-algebraic) stratified figures. That would give a point-free axiomatics of tame topology, which does not seem to exist explicitly.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine but careful lemma in an unpublished axiomatization of tame topology. The orthogonality/polarity approach is mildly interesting and parallels point-free topology, but the page itself contains only an elementary case split and a natural separation hypothesis.
transcription_corrections: The index set in both unions reads 'Z ∈ cosupp°(X)' (or 'cosupp(X)'), not 'compl(X)'.
Crossed-out text after 'Z ∈ M' is '∁|X|' (correctly marked as deleted). In the line 'i.e. ∃Z ≤ X', the whole line is struck through.

Marginal note reads roughly: 'C'est trop fort, il est plus raisonnable d'écrire Z |°| X (pour inclure p.ex. les ensembles [?] définis par des inégalités, et notamment les inégalités)'. The reading 'morphismes fidèles' is doubtful; the point concerns sets defined by inequalities.
'ce qui signifie, puisque ∂X = ⋃_{Z<X}|Z|°, que' is the intended reading of the line after the struck-out one.
